name: FIFA World Cup 26 Brand Manual
tagline: Official 184-page FIFA World Cup 26 assets brand manual, Edition 12
description: The complete official brand manual for the FIFA World Cup 26 tournament — 'ASSETS BRAND MANUAL, EDITION 12, JUNE 2025' — shared as a public 43 MB A4-landscape PDF on Google Drive. It documents the Official Emblem (design story, technical set-up, exclusion areas, metallic reproduction, lineart, on-screen rules), the Official Slogan and its lock-ups, host-country emblems, the wordmark, official typography, stakeholder composite logos, designation logos, volunteer / qualifiers / final-draw logos, a 16-column layout grid, office templates, logo strips, and the approval and artwork-coding process. Useful as a primary-source reference for how a top-tier event identity is specified in full rigour, not as reusable code or assets.
agent_guidance: Treat this as a study reference for identity-system structure, never as assets you may ship — every mark in it is FIFA-trademarked and the manual states explicit legal-notice and approval requirements. Mine it when a user asks what a serious brand book must cover: it gives you a real section skeleton (emblem, slogan, lock-ups, wordmark, typography, stakeholder logos, layout grid, office templates, approval flow) plus real colour breakdowns given as CMYK / RGB / HEX / PMS / TCX / RAL / NCS. It is a 43 MB, 184-page encrypted PDF on a personal Google Drive link, so extract what you need once rather than re-fetching, and expect the link to rot.
why_it_matters: Full official brand manuals for events of this scale almost never circulate publicly, so this is a rare primary source for how emblem, lock-up, typography, and grid rules are actually specified end to end.
notable_for: Event typeface FWC26 with Noto Sans as support
evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1crONZDtndDmOaXIgxdfChT2JvAgsesiy/view (WebFetch showed a sign-in prompt; direct curl returned HTTP 200 with title 'FIFA 2026 Brand guideline .pdf'), https://drive.usercontent.google.com/download?id=1crONZDtndDmOaXIgxdfChT2JvAgsesiy&export=download (downloaded 43,419,502 bytes, PDF 1.7, 184 pages; table of contents, emblem colour, metallic colour and typography pages read with pdftotext)

name: Aarzoo Aly — Work (Cosmos)
tagline: Public Cosmos cluster of ~244 editorial and typographic references
description: A public cluster named 'Work' on Cosmos, the visual-inspiration platform, curated by @aarzooaly (154 followers, bio 'Focused on Editorial and Typographic Aesthetic'). The embedded payload reports 244 items; the first page alone loads 34 CDN images. It is a saved image board, not a portfolio site and not a case-study collection — the value is the curation angle (editorial layout, type-led composition), not any accompanying writing.
pricing_detail: Browsing a public cluster is free; saving to your own cluster needs a Cosmos account.
agent_guidance: Use this only as a mood source for editorial and type-driven layout direction — there is no text, no source attribution and no code on the page, so you cannot cite it for a technique or a spec. The cluster HTML is server-rendered and the image URLs live on cdn.cosmos.so, so you can harvest thumbnails programmatically, but the grid pages in on scroll, meaning one fetch gives you roughly 34 of the 244 items. Pair it with a real type or grid reference before you make layout decisions; a moodboard is evidence of taste, not of a system.
why_it_matters: A single curator's board is only as good as the eye behind it, and this one is narrowly and consistently editorial — which makes it more useful for direction-setting than a broad, unfiltered gallery.
notable_for: Curator bio states the filter explicitly

name: Brand Assets Generator
tagline: Canvas generator for technical-diagram brand imagery, PNG or SVG
description: A personal single-page canvas tool by Yordan Stoyanov that composes technical, blueprint-style brand imagery — plotted points, dashed circles, crosshairs, coordinate labels and pseudo-telemetry captions such as 'PARAMETRIC.GEN' and 'GEOMETRIC.SYS'. It ships four views (Circles, Studio, Geo Tool, Hero) with six draw modes (Orbital, Radial, Arcs, Lissajous, Constellation, Drawing), three motion types (Morph, Draw, Pulse), six palettes (White/Dark, Black/Light, Gold/Dark, Green/Dark, Cool Dark, Warm Grey), and sliders for grid divisions, turbulence, stroke weight, overlay opacity and a noise/texture layer. Output exports as PNG or SVG at seven built-in presets. It is an image factory for brand and social artwork, not a component library.

templates.name: Portrait 3:4 (1200x1600)
templates.purpose: Portrait export preset in the Studio view

pricing_detail: Free, no account and no visible paywall.
agent_guidance: Reach for this when a user wants a technical/FUI/blueprint hero or social image and you would otherwise fake it with gradients — the SVG export means the output stays crisp and editable, so prefer SVG over PNG whenever it is going into a build. Do not try to script it: it is a Vite SPA that ships an empty 2 KB body and renders everything into a canvas client-side, so there is no API, no route to deep-link a preset, and a headless fetch returns nothing. There is also no stated licence or attribution line, so ask the user before putting an export into anything commercial.
why_it_matters: It hits a specific and hard-to-fake look — parametric, instrument-panel geometry — that most gradient and pattern generators cannot produce, and it exports vector rather than a flat bitmap.
notable_for: Four views: Circles, Studio, Geo Tool, Hero
Six draw modes including Lissajous and Constellation
PNG and SVG export at seven size presets

name: Instant Domain Search
tagline: Keystroke-speed domain availability across 800+ TLDs, with a free MCP server
description: An ICANN-accredited registrar whose front end checks domain availability in real time as you type, across 800+ extensions, with dedicated landing pages for .ai, .io, .com, .net, .org, .info, .app, .co, .me, .online, .xyz and .dev. Beyond plain search it ships an AI domain generator, a business-name generator, bulk search for up to 5,000 domains with CSV import/export and multi-registrar price comparison, aftermarket search across Afternic / Sedo / Atom / Sav, an expired and pending-delete domain browser, a Raycast extension, and a domain directory. Most importantly for agents, it exposes a free, no-auth MCP server at api.instantdomainsearch.com with search_domains, generate_domain_variations and check_domain_availability.
pricing_detail: Search, the generators, bulk search and the MCP server are free with no account; revenue comes from domain registration as an ICANN-accredited registrar and from aftermarket referrals.
agent_guidance: This is the one naming tool you can actually call rather than screenshot: connect the streamable-HTTP MCP endpoint at https://api.instantdomainsearch.com/mcp/streamable-http — no key, no auth, responses around 10 ms — and use check_domain_availability to verify before you ever suggest a product name to a user. Pair generate_domain_variations with a username check so you do not ship a name whose .com is taken or whose handle is gone. Watch two things: it is a registrar, so the 'best deal' ordering is commercially motivated, and availability is a point-in-time answer — re-check immediately before the user registers.
why_it_matters: It is the rare naming utility built for machines as well as humans; a free unauthenticated MCP endpoint turns 'is this name free' from a manual browser task into a tool call inside the naming loop.
notable_for: Free no-auth MCP server, three tools
Bulk search up to 5,000 domains with CSV
Raycast extension and Cursor deeplink install
evidence: https://instantdomainsearch.com (WebFetch), https://instantdomainsearch.com/mcp (WebFetch — endpoint URL, the three tool names, Cursor deeplink and the 'free tool' statement)

name: Instant Username Search
tagline: Checks one handle against 100+ social platforms as you type
description: A single-purpose web app that checks whether a username is free on more than 100 social media and developer platforms, updating results live as you type rather than after a submit. It is the handle-side companion to a domain check when you are locking down a new brand identity. The source is open on GitHub (React, GPL-3.0, 225 stars) but that repository was archived on 2024-04-01, so the hosted site is running frozen code.
pricing_detail: Free; the site solicits optional donations (Buy Me a Coffee, Bitcoin).
agent_guidance: Hand this to the user as a link — do not try to fetch or scrape it, because Cloudflare returns 403 to non-browser clients (verified). Use it as the second half of a naming check right after a domain lookup: a name is only safe when the .com and the main handles are both free. Treat its verdicts as advisory, not authoritative: the upstream repo has been archived since April 2024, so platform checks that changed their signup endpoints since then can report a stale answer, and it will not know about any platform launched after that date.
why_it_matters: Handle availability is the step most naming workflows skip, and this covers 100+ platforms in one keystroke-speed pass instead of a dozen manual signup-form probes.
notable_for: 100+ platforms checked live as you type
evidence: https://instantusername.com (WebFetch HTTP 403; curl with a browser UA also 403, body was a Cloudflare 'Attention Required' interstitial), WebSearch for corroboration, GitHub API repos/instantusername/instant-username-search (225 stars, GPL-3.0, archived, pushed 2024-04-01)

name: Etymonline
tagline: Etymology dictionary of English word origins, running since 2001
description: The Online Etymology Dictionary, written and maintained by Douglas Harper since 2001 with Talia Felix as associate editor since 2021. It gives the origin and recorded history of English words, phrases and idioms — what a word meant and sounded like centuries back — rather than a present-day definition, describing itself as 'a map of the wheel-ruts of modern English'. It browses A–Z, and ships a Chrome extension plus iOS and Android apps; a premium tier removes ads and adds offline access, notes, translation and sync.
pricing_detail: Premium is $4.99/month or $17.99/year; student and educator rate is $8.99 for the first year then $17.99/year. The dictionary itself is free with ads.
agent_guidance: Use this during naming and brand-voice work, not during UI work: when a user is choosing a product or feature name, check the root here so you can tell them what the word actually carried before marketing got to it — and catch the ones with an unflattering or unintended history. Pair it with Instant Domain Search and Instant Username Search to close the loop from meaning to availability. There is no API and no llms.txt, so fetch individual word pages directly and cite the page; also be aware the entries are one scholar's synthesis, so treat a contested etymology as a claim rather than a fact.
why_it_matters: Naming decisions that survive scrutiny start from real word history, and this has been the reference practitioners actually use for that since 2001.
notable_for: Continuously edited since 2001 by Douglas Harper
Chrome extension plus iOS and Android apps
No API — fetch word pages directly
